transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I just feel wound up almost all the time. It's like my body is constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen. It doesn't really seem to matter what I'm doing, either—even when I'm just sitting at my desk working, or trying to enjoy dance night, I just have this physical tension that I can't seem to shake.
How long have you been feeling this constant tension and on-edge feeling—days, weeks, or months?
It's been months. I'd say... probably about nine months now. It really started back when my condo loan started moving toward foreclosure.

Since this started, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different areas of your life—like health, work, or relationships—or does your worry stay mostly focused on the foreclosure situation?

No, it definitely doesn't stay on the condo anymore. It really just... jumps around. I'll find myself worrying about whether my cousin is upset with me, or I'll stress over whether I'm going to make a mistake on a support call at work. And then it shifts to other things, like how I'll ever manage to save money or just... move forward with my life. It seems like it's always something different.
Along with this constant worry and tension, have you noticed other symptoms like feeling easily fatigued, trouble concentrating, irritability, or difficulty sleeping?

Well, the sleep is definitely a big issue. Most nights I get into bed completely exhausted, but my brain just won't shut off. It keeps replaying, you know, the loan notices, work tickets, or just... things I might have missed that day. I usually end up lying there awake until 2 or 3 in the morning. And even when I finally do get to sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or your mind going blank during the day, like when you're at work or trying to focus on a task?

Yeah, definitely. It happens a lot at work. I'll be right in the middle of writing a script, or helping someone on a call—whether it's in English or Spanish—and suddenly I realize I'm just staring at the screen. My mind just drifts off to everything that could go wrong, and I completely lose the thread of what I was doing. It makes it really hard to focus on the task in front of me.
Have you noticed that you've been more irritable or quick to snap at others over these past several months?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I definitely feel stressed out all the time, but I don't think I'm taking it out on anyone else. I haven't been snapping at my friends or the people I help at work. It's mostly just... internal, I guess. I just keep it to myself.
Have you noticed feeling easily fatigued or experiencing muscle tension, like sore shoulders or clenched jaw, during this time?

Not really. I mean, I'm definitely tired during the day just from the lack of sleep, like I mentioned, but I wouldn't say I get fatigued easily from doing normal things. And as for the muscle tension... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. My shoulders feel fine, and I don't think I've been clenching my jaw or anything.
Has this constant worry and tension been significant enough to interfere with your daily life—like your work performance, relationships, or ability to enjoy activities?

Yeah, it really has. At work, I've actually started falling behind on my support tickets. I just... I end up double-checking really simple tasks so much that my coworkers have had to step in and pick up the slack for me. And outside of work, it's affecting things too. I've skipped several of my dance nights recently, and, um, some mentoring sessions I usually do. I just feel way too overwhelmed to even show up right now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports excessive, uncontrollable worry across multiple domains (finances, work performance, relationships) persisting for approximately 9 months, exceeding the 6-month threshold for GAD. Associated symptoms include sleep disturbance (difficulty falling asleep, non-restorative sleep), concentration difficulties/mind going blank, and pervasive physical tension/feeling 'on edge,' meeting criteria of at least 3 associated symptoms. This has caused clear functional impairment at work (falling behind, needing coworker support) and socially (avoiding dance nights, mentoring). While an initial stressor (condo foreclosure) triggered the symptoms, the worry has generalized beyond this single stressor and persists independent of it, making Adjustment Disorder less fitting. No manic, psychotic, or trauma-specific re-experiencing symptoms were reported, and irritability/muscle tension were specifically denied, but sufficient criteria are still met for GAD.
